scenes.title: The outcome
points: Wrap existing source without erasing it
Establish a retained baseline
Real session excerpts; edited transcript replay

dialogue.speaker: sam
dialogue.text: You're going to rewrite a popular C plus plus library automatically?

dialogue.speaker: litai
dialogue.text: This course shows phased adoption of an existing repository. The goal is useful evidence now, with no fiction that old source instantly becomes specification-led or safe to discard. These are edited transcript replays of real sessions, not raw screen recordings. Remote-worker steps are a walkthrough.

scenes.title: Before conversion
points: Confirm a Git or equivalent recovery point
Keep unrelated changes and credentials safe
Inspect before authorizing mutation

dialogue.speaker: litai
dialogue.text: Before converting, preserve a recovery point and identify any sensitive material. Conversion is a real repository mutation, so inspect the plan first and authorize the apply only after reviewing its effects.

scenes.title: Phase zero: inspect
points: TinyXML2 at Git commit 8224e427
Detected C++, Python, CMake, and CTest
Readiness: ready; no catalog gaps

dialogue.speaker: sam
dialogue.text: I already have a Makefile and CMake. What will you discover?

dialogue.speaker: litai
dialogue.text: Our actual demo uses TinyXML2, a public C plus plus XML parser, pinned at Git commit 8224e427. Read-only adopt detected C plus plus, Python, CMake, CTest, and no catalog gaps. It also proposed the source moves before writing anything.

scenes.title: Phase one: wrapped
points: Apply only after reviewing the plan
Legacy source remains release authority
The framework adds wrappers and parity evidence

dialogue.speaker: litai
dialogue.text: After acknowledgement, the harness wraps the tree and records what it preserved. The first stage is wrapped. Original source remains release authority; the new specification surface is not yet a replacement.

scenes.title: Live C++ baseline
points: Original build and test commands still run
CMake built the library and xmltest
CTest reported one passing test

dialogue.speaker: litai
dialogue.text: The conversion harness actually ran TinyXML2's existing CMake build and CTest command in disposable custody. The library and xmltest built, and CTest reported one passing test. This preserves a concrete baseline, not just a diagram.

scenes.title: A production gap, reproduced
points: CTest 4.4 reports a newer all-passed summary
Old parser rejected the exact count
New regression covers both CTest summary formats

dialogue.speaker: sam
dialogue.text: CTest passed. Why won't you mark it retained?

dialogue.speaker: litai
dialogue.text: Our first retained run failed even though CTest passed: the old parser did not recognize the newer all-passed summary. We fixed the framework adapter and tested both summary formats, including zero and unknown counts. The real TinyXML2 rerun now produces an exact one-test receipt.

scenes.title: Publish proof, advance the stage
points: Real retained harness rerun: 1 passed, 0 failed
Publish the finalized receipt before advancing
Stage: retained; authority: original-source

dialogue.speaker: sam
dialogue.text: Couldn't you just ignore that counting error?

dialogue.speaker: litai
dialogue.text: We did not ignore the counting error. After fixing it, we reran the actual CMake and CTest harness, published its finalized receipt, and advanced TinyXML2 from wrapped to retained. Original source remains release authority. We have not claimed drafted, qualified, or specification-led shipping.

scenes.title: Phase three: drafted
points: Translate source into reviewable intent
Review behavior and target choices with humans
Move one boundary at a time

dialogue.speaker: litai
dialogue.text: Next, derive candidate specifications from the existing source, then review them as product intent. This is a draft, not proof. Move one Component boundary at a time and keep the original implementation available for parity checks.

scenes.title: Phase four: qualified
points: Clean spec-only regeneration
Build, current tests, and independent parity
Authority changes only with current trusted proof

dialogue.speaker: litai
dialogue.text: Qualification compares clean regenerations against the retained baseline. Historical clean runs alone do not transfer release authority. Only current, trusted lifecycle evidence bound to the exact lock can authorize specification authority.

scenes.title: What improves early
points: Known baseline and explicit gaps
Repeatable build and test evidence
Safer agent changes and easier handoffs

dialogue.speaker: litai
dialogue.text: The first benefits arrive before any rewrite: a visible baseline, explicit catalog gaps, and a precise explanation when test evidence is incomplete. Teams can review intent and agent changes without losing the ability to run the old application.

scenes.title: What takes longer
points: Not an automatic native rewrite
No guarantee of immediate speed or quality gains
Release authority changes last, not first

dialogue.speaker: sam
dialogue.text: So when do I actually get to ship from the specification?

dialogue.speaker: litai
dialogue.text: Adoption is not an automatic source-to-specification rewrite, nor a promise of instant speedups. The pragmatic path is to retain working behavior, build evidence one boundary at a time, and promote authority only when the independent gates pass.
